atoms.b:
The USA in World War II
During World War II (1939-1945), the ((Allied_forces)) fought against ((Germany)) and its supporters, Italy and Japan. The US joined the Allies after the Japanese had attacked their military base at ((Pearl_Harbor)), Hawaii, in 1941.

The German forces surrendered eventually, but Japan refused to do the same. As a result, the USA destroyed the Japanese cities Hiroshima and Nagasaki with ((atomic_bombs)) in 1945, which ensured Japan's ((surrender)) and the end of the war, but also cost the lives of hundreds of thousands of ((civilians)).

International relations after WWII
In 1947, President Harry S. Truman announced the USA would aid any ((nations)) endangered by communism. Known as the Truman Doctrine, this increased tensions between the USA and the ((Soviet)) Union and initiated the Cold War (1947-1991), characterized by the two nations threatening each other with ((nuclear_weapons)).

When Vietnam split into a communist North and an anti-communist South, the United States supported the South out of fear of another communist nation rising to power. From 1964-1975, the USA sent troops to fight in the ((Vietnam_War)). Over a million people are estimated to have died, more than 50,000 of them American soldiers. Many Americans opposed the war, and with North Vietnam's ((victory)), they felt like the deaths and injuries of their peers had been pointless. Even today, it is still considered a great tragedy.

The Soviet Union ((collapsed)) in 1991, marking the end of the Cold War.

On September 11, 2001, terrorists from the Islamist al-Qaeda organization seized control over four ((planes)) and flew three of them into the ((World_Trade_Center)) and the Pentagon, killing not only the passengers on the planes, but also many people in and around the buildings. Known as ((9/11)), this caused the USA to initiate a “war on terror” against Islamist militant groups, during which they ((invaded)) and attacked various countries in West Asia and parts of Africa.
